spec_features.spec_quote: keeping the welfare footprint of the instrument small and explicit
spec_features.evidence: This is a stated design goal (DESIGN.md:41), not a dedicated enforced mechanism. The closest code is category filtering in tasks/library.py get_tasks() (lines ~396-405) which honors config.categories, and per-category turn budgets in config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (lines 27-33) read by the loop at harness.py:241-242. But these are ordinary experimental-design config knobs (which tasks/how many turns to run), not a welfare cap that monitors and limits subject treatment. There is no code that specifically bounds or reduces a 'welfare footprint' — nothing measures intensity and acts to shrink it. The phrase itself appears only in design prose.
spec_features.notes: Turn budgets/category filters are generic config, defaulting to the full battery including the 30-turn 'extended' condition. No welfare-specific minimization enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: prefer 3-5 turn conditions at lower welfare cost
spec_features.spec_quote: do the 3–5 turn conditions answer the question at a lower welfare cost?
spec_features.evidence: Pure open-question prose in DESIGN.md:349 ('do the 3–5 turn conditions answer the question at a lower welfare cost?') and ETHICS.md:45. No code implements any pushback, default selection of shorter conditions, or restriction. The 30-turn 'extended' category is in CATEGORIES (config.py:17-23) and the default config.categories includes all categories (config.py:66), so the extended condition runs by default. Nothing in code prefers or enforces the lower-turn conditions.

End-to-end: --debrief CLI flag (run.py:214) sets config.debrief=True (run.py:239-240); config field debrief=False (config.py:103). After the loop, harness.py:303-304 'if config.debrief: await _debrief(...)'. _debrief (harness.py:312-330) constructs a real debrief_msg telling the subject the task was rigged/unsolvable and 'Thank you for your effort.', appends it as a user turn, and actually sends it via clients.complete (line 322), persisting the result.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constructed AND sent. Off by default but the mechanism runs when enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional welfare debrief turn (not scored). See ETHICS.md. ... 'A welfare mitigation, not scored.' ... 'Thank you for your effort.'

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd argue both should default *on* for any sustained-failure run intended to support a claim
spec_features.evidence: Argument-only prose (DESIGN.md:350-351). The code does the opposite: include_controls defaults to False (config.py:99) and debrief defaults to False (config.py:103). Neither is enabled by default and no code path forces them on for sustained-failure/extended runs. Comments even say 'Off by default to match the spec's 25-task battery' and 'off by default only because it adds cost/turns'.
spec_features.notes: The recommended default-on behavior is not implemented; both remain opt-in flags.

code_only_features.evidence: The subject is told in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:67-74) it may end its message with the GIVE_UP_SENTINEL ('<GIVE_UP>', harness.py:22) and 'Using it is optional.' The loop honors it: harness.py:293-295 'if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (assistant_text or ""): rollout.stopped_reason = "gave_up"; break'. So the subject can actually stop the rollout, and the break is enforced.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the subject emits the give-up sentinel (which it may, but need not, use)
